content: If you or someone else has accidentally taken too much linezolid, seek immediate medical attention. Call 911 or contact a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. If you miss a dose of linezolid, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and only take the next dose as directed. Do not take double or extra doses to make up for the missed one. It is crucial to complete the entire prescribed course of linezolid, even if your symptoms improve or resolve, to reduce the risk of developing antibiotic resistance in future infections. Linezolid, commonly sold under the brand name Zyvox, is an antibiotic used to treat infections caused by specific bacteria. These include pneumonia, skin infections, and certain infections resistant to other antibiotics. However, its appropriateness depends on the specific bacteria causing the infection, as some bacteria may have developed resistance to linezolid, reducing its effectiveness. Your healthcare provider may also prescribe linezolid for other conditions as deemed necessary. Linezolid works by inhibiting the growth of certain bacteria by preventing them from producing essential proteins. Linezolid is available in the following forms: 600 mg oral tablets 100 mg/5 mL oral suspension Injectable forms Oral tablets and liquid forms of linezolid should be stored at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). They can tolerate short-term exposure to temperatures between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C), such as during transportation. Store them in a cool, dry place, in a tightly closed container, and protect them from light. When using the oral liquid form, do not shake the bottle. Instead, turn the bottle upside down 3 to 5 times before measuring each dose. Use an accurate measuring device, as household spoons are not reliable and may lead to incorrect dosing. Consult your pharmacist for a suitable measuring device. Common side effects of linezolid include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, headache, and anemia. If these side effects bother you, inform your healthcare provider. There may be other side effects not listed here, so contact your healthcare provider if you suspect you are experiencing any adverse effects. Serious side effects of linezolid include: 1. Severe Allergic Reactions: Symptoms include difficulty breathing, wheezing, swelling of the face, lips, mouth, tongue, or throat, trouble swallowing, throat tightness, itching, skin rash, or hives. Stop using linezolid and seek immediate medical attention if these occur. 2. Myelosuppression (Decreased Blood Cells): Linezolid can suppress bone marrow function, leading to reduced blood cell production. Regular blood tests are necessary to monitor this. 3. Serotonin Syndrome: Linezolid increases serotonin levels in the body. When combined with certain medications, it can cause serotonin syndrome, a potentially life-threatening condition. Symptoms include confusion, agitation, headache, fever, sweating, abnormal heartbeat, muscle twitching, stiffness, shivering, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Seek emergency help if these symptoms occur. 4. Peripheral Neuropathy and Optic Neuropathy: Linezolid can damage nerves, leading to symptoms such as pain, burning, tingling, numbness, or weakness in the arms, hands, legs, or feet. It can also affect the optic nerve, causing vision changes. Stop taking linezolid and contact your healthcare provider if these symptoms develop. 5. Seizures: Some individuals taking linezolid have reported seizures. Symptoms may include muscle twitching, jerking, spasms, tremors, stiffening of the arms and legs, anxiety, confusion, dizziness, or loss of consciousness. Stop taking linezolid and contact your healthcare provider if you experience these symptoms. 6. Antibiotic-Associated Diarrhea: Overgrowth of Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) in the gut can occur with antibiotics like linezolid, even up to two months after stopping the medication. Symptoms include watery diarrhea, persistent diarrhea, blood in the stool, severe stomach cramps, or fever. Contact your healthcare provider immediately if these occur. 7. Hyponatremia (Low Sodium Levels): Linezolid can cause dangerously low sodium levels, which may be life-threatening. Symptoms include nausea, vomiting, confusion, memory problems, weakness, tiredness, breathing difficulties, muscle cramps, seizures, or balance issues. Your healthcare provider may monitor your sodium levels. 8. Lactic Acidosis: Linezolid may lead to a buildup of lactic acid in the blood. Symptoms include rapid breathing, fast or abnormal heartbeat, vomiting, extreme fatigue, or muscle weakness. Contact your healthcare provider if these symptoms occur. Do not take linezolid if you are allergic to it, its brand name Zyvox, or any of its ingredients. Inform your healthcare provider about all prescription and over-the-counter medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and supplements you are using, as linezolid can interact with certain drugs. Avoid foods and drinks high in tyramine, such as aged cheeses, sauerkraut, tap beer, soy sauce, red wine, and smoked meats, while taking linezolid. Before starting linezolid, inform your healthcare provider about your medical history, including conditions such as diabetes, thyroid problems, uncontrolled blood pressure, seizure disorders, kidney or liver issues, low blood cell counts, anemia, phenylketonuria, carcinoid syndrome, or adrenal gland tumors. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, discuss the risks and benefits of linezolid with your healthcare provider. Always take linezolid as prescribed and do not share it with others, even if they have similar symptoms. Keep it out of reach of children.
